title: Rate governor islanding and progressive absorption playbook for limiter outages
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: During a recent regional limiter outage (INC-2026-03-01-05) we observed noisy neighbor amplification where a single overloaded region caused cascading quota thrashing in adjacent regions. Current limiter behavior (hard deny + global fallback) caused large numbers of customers to see sudden 429s and then long tail latency when traffic retried.

Goal: Create an operational playbook and runtime changes that make limiter outages graceful and SLO-friendly by: 1) islanding the affected region quickly to stop oscillation; 2) progressively absorbing some of the failed region's load into healthy regions using weighted, SLO-aware admission (progressive absorption); 3) rehydrating circuits gradually (circuit rehydration) with tenant-aware fairness credits to avoid permanent starvation.

Scope: design, implementation, and rollout of the "Rate Governor" behavior in the admission path plus runbook updates to Console and SRE pager playbooks. Affects hosted and dedicated deployments; Private deployments can adopt the same principles but may need cluster-specific config.

Non-goals: full redesign of quota accounting or billing changes for this iteration.

Key design principles: minimize SLO violations for high-priority tenants, avoid global cascading retries, preserve proportional fairness for tenants during absorption windows, and provide clear telemetry and rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated regional outage tests show no more than 3% additional p95 latency violations across healthy regions during a 5-minute islanding window (compared to baseline)
Progressive absorption limits per-tenant amplification: no tenant is admitted >2x their normal rate share during absorption windows without explicit override
Circuit rehydration feature prevents immediate retry storms: reintegration is throttled with exponentially increasing admission and observed safe-to-open flag
Runbook documented in Confluence and linked from Console incident view
End-to-end integration tests and a chaos run against staging (multiregion) complete without SLO regression
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'rate_governor_v1' in staging
Stage 1: Canary in staging cluster (single region) with synthetic traffic injection and chaos job (3 days)
Stage 2: Canary in multi-region staging with simulated region failover (5 days)
Stage 3: Gradual rollout to low-traffic prod region (10% traffic for 24h), monitor Console SLO dashboard
Stage 4: 50% traffic across cross-region, monitor for tenant unfairness signals and token-level errors
Stage 5: Full enablement with rollback to 'legacy-fallback' if error budget exceeded (configurable threshold)
Require on-call SRE presence during prod canaries and first 24h of full enablement
test_plan: Unit tests for admission logic and tenant credit accounting
Property tests for absorption algorithm ensuring monotonic bounds
Integration test: fail region A, verify region B admits <= configured absorption share and global SLOs not violated
Chaos test: intermittent circuit rehydration flaps while running progressive absorption
Load test: 2x synthetic burst from 10 tenants with different priority levels; verify weighted fairness and no starvation
comments: 2026-02-11 - Ava Chen: Spiked initial design. Decided to pursue 'islanding' (immediate soft-deny of new sessions for the affected region) vs hard global cutover. Rationale: limits retry amplification and isolates oscillation. Added initial sequence diagrams to Confluence link.

2026-02-18 - Diego Martinez: POC completed for weighted absorption algorithm. POC notes: used tenant score = historical avg qps * priority_multiplier, absorption share computed as min(global_headroom * region_weight, per_tenant_cap). Observed edge-case where very low-usage tenants could be starved; added transient credit allocator to avoid starvation.
2026-02-25 - Design review (K. Patel): UX needs: show 'absorbed traffic' metric on tenant dashboard and expose per-tenant override for enterprise support. Action: PM to scope console surface.

2026-03-01 - Incident retrospective (INC-2026-03-01-05): root cause was datastore GC + limiter lease drift. Learning: admission should not rely on single lease refresh for global fallback decision. Added a secondary lease health indicator and degraded-mode behavior.
2026-03-04 - PR feedback (R. Singh): asked to add additional telemetry tags: region_island_id, absorption_batch_id, and circuit_rehydrate_epoch. Action: added tracing spans and logs.

2026-03-07 - QA (M. Lopez): Integration test found a race: rehydration window overlapped absorption and allowed >2x admission for a tenant. Mitigation: make rehydration warmup observe live token issuance and require two consecutive safe epochs before doubling admit rate.
2026-03-10 - Diego Martinez: Implemented exponential backoff for rehydration; added feature toggle and initial chaos test scenarios. Ready for staging canary next week.
incident_notes: INC-2026-03-01-05: During a 17-minute limiter control plane outage in eu-west-1, we saw 40% of global 429s originate from downstream retries triggered by global fallback policy.
Observation: global hard-fallback amplified peak QPS due to retry storms; downstream rate limiters in other regions responded by throwing 429s, creating oscillation.
Fix applied: emergency rollout of region-level hard islanding and manual traffic steering reduced 429 rate by ~65% within 3 minutes (postmortem link in Confluence).
Long-term: this ticket encapsulates the automated version of those manual mitigations plus fairness mechanisms to prevent tenant starvation.
